It’s been awhile since we have offered coffee from Yemen. The country has been devastated by a civil war and coffee production has obviously greatly diminished. Amidst the turmoil, Fatoum Muslot, daughter of long time Yemeni exporter Ali Hebah Muslot, has set out to improve the standard of living for her coffee growing community and to restore Yemeni coffee cultivation. We have two small microlots of their coffee. The first we are offering is Mocha Harazi from the Sana’a region which includes and supports 141 coffee-growing families. This lot is a sun-dried natural process of Dawaeri & Jadi varieties. These are rare, delicious coffees and we love the dark chocolate, blackberry, and warm spice flavors we are tasting.

Raspberry & Orange. Special Special.


This fresh new offering from Papua New Guinea hits your palate upfront with flavors of clean raspberry and finishes off with tart orange notes. It's grown on a collection of small farms in the Kindeng Municipality in the Jawaka Province - which is within the very fertile Wahgi Valley. The cherries are first sent to the Kindeng wet mill where they are thoroughly dried, and then they are sent off to the Kagamuga Mill where they are hulled, sorted and bagged. Final destination: your kitchen. Enjoy!

This coffee comes from a washing station located at the base of Mount Kenya called the Kangunu Coffee Factory where a collective of farmers gather to process their coffees. The farmers are encouraged to become members of a cooperative, which markets and sells coffee on the whole communities behalf.

This region is known for their 72 hour fermentation process that continually utilizes fresh water to remove any lingering fruit. The water is sourced from the nearby Kangunu stream and placed into reservoir tanks by electrical pumps. For this wet-processing method, the factory uses a disc pulper with three sets of discs to remove the skin and fruit from the inner parchment layer that is protecting the green coffee bean. After pulping, the coffee is fermented overnight to break down the sugars, before it is cleaned, soaked and spread out on the raised drying tables and can take anywhere from 7-15 days to dry.

raw.description: The Alto San Juan Micromill is a family farm that has been brought to life by its current young owner, Diego Abarca, as he turns it into a thriving business. As Alto San Juan continues to grow, they have been able to experiment with coffees while having better control over their product. This allows them to not only concentrate on washed coffees but experiment with honey and natural processes, as well. We are excited to join them on this journey by offering their Honey process, grown at 1600 masl, and look out for a Natural process from the San Juan Micromill in the near future.
